entities.summary: Diuma was the first Bishop of Mercia in the Anglo-Saxon Kingdom of Mercia, during the Early Middle Ages. Born into a noble family, Diuma rose to prominence in the 7th century AD, when Mercia was a powerful and influential region in Anglo-Saxon England. As Bishop, Diuma played a crucial role in shaping the religious and cultural identity of the Anglo-Saxon people, and his legacy continued to influence the development of Christianity in England for centuries to come. Diuma's leadership and diplomacy helped to establish Mercia as a major player in European politics, and his reputation as a wise and just leader endured long after his death in 658 CE. The Bishop's influence can still be seen in the many churches and monasteries that he founded, and his legacy serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and community in shaping the course of human history.
